Priya to schedule 2-week Dedicated POC and send POC checklist by 2025-08-18
Lumera to confirm internal stakeholders for procurement by 2025-08-22
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send SOC2 Type II report, recent pentest summary, and whitepaper on BYOK - due 2025-08-20

summary: Intro call to capture Lumera's security and hosting constraints for a potential Redwood deployment. Primary concerns: key management (BYOK/HSM), SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, audit log granularity and retention, SOC2/ISO evidence, and data residency/retention policies. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and next steps for POC and documentation handoff.
topics: Encryption at rest/in transit + KMS/BYOK/HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-15 16:00 UTC | Duration ~42m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (SE), Mateo Ruiz (CS), Evan Morales (Lumera Head Infra), Sasha Kim (Lumera Security), Dr. Marie Chen (CTO), Omar Patel (Procurement)

Summary (auto): capture security constraints for regulated EU workload, determine whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private pipeline needed; surface SOC2 and KMS requirements, agree next steps for POC and deliverables.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan with Redwood inference — appreciate you taking the time. quick around the room?
[00:18] Evan: Evan here, head of infra at Lumera. we're evaluating inference vendors for a roadmap project, main constraints are data residency and keys.
[00:30] Sasha: Sasha, security engineer — i'll own risk questions, compliance, and the SOC stuff.
[00:37] Marie: Marie Chen, cto, mostly listening but want to make sure latency/cost tradeoffs don't blow up the budget.
[00:45] Jordan: great, thanks. priya and mateo from my side, priya will run the technical bits, mateo helps onboard and will coordinate the POC.
[01:05] Priya: hi all — quick note, i'll probably ask about dataset handling, audit logs, and key management.
[01:15] Omar: Omar from procurement, i'll poke on contracts and timelines.
[01:22] Jordan: cool, objective for today is to map Lumera's compliance gates — soc2, iso, sso, rbacs, k-m-s — and decide initial path: hosted, dedicated, or private. also agree immediate artifacts we need to share.
[01:40] Sasha: first Q — do you have SOC2 type II? and iso? what's the current compliance posture for hosted?
[01:50] Jordan: yes, we have SOC2 Type II for the hosted service, we also have an ISO 27001 program underway — i can share the certificate status and the scoping doc. note: our Dedicated customers can get additional SLAs and slightly different data handling commitments; Private (VPC/on-prem) is available for air-gapped regulated workloads.
[02:18] Sasha: do you have pen test reports and do you allow customers to run their own red team?
[02:25] Jordan: we have a recent pentest summary and are happy to share redacted findings. for customers we often allow scoped tests under NDA and coordinate with our security team. i'll attach the pentest summary and the process doc.
[02:40] Evan: key management — our security team requires BYOK and HSM-backed keys for production. how does Redwood handle KMS?
[02:50] Priya: we integrate with cloud KMS options — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault. For Dedicated and Private we support BYOK workflows and HSM-backed key material; for Hosted we can offer customer key wrapping using KMS, but full BYOK with HSM trust separation is usually on Dedicated/Private.
[03:15] Sasha: so hosted uses your managed keys by default? can we do a key encryption key (KEK) in our KMS that wraps the data keys?
[03:24] Priya: yes, hosted by default uses Redwood-managed key material. we do offer envelope encryption where you provide a KEK from your KMS to wrap the DEKs — that covers many customers. for the strict HSM-only BYOK model where you hold sole custody of the key and we never see unwrapped keys, that is designated for Dedicated or Private deployments.
[03:50] Marie: what's the control plane separation look like for Dedicated — is the control plane still hosted?
[03:58] Jordan: good question — Dedicated customers have a logically isolated runtime and committed capacity; the control plane remains in our managed service but we offer private control plane options for Private deployments. we can discuss a private control plane if you need it for compliance.
[04:20] Evan: data residency — we have EU customers and need data to stay in eu-west region; can you pin model inference to region and ensure logs don't leave region?
[04:33] Priya: yes, we support region pinning on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we have EU regions where data residency is provided; audit logs can be configured to store in your region or sent to your SIEM via secure log forwarding (syslog/secure forwarder).
[04:55] Sasha: audit logs — what granularity? token-level? request payloads? do you keep full transcripts?
[05:04] Priya: by default we store request/response metadata and high-level payloads for x days (we call it 90 days standard), including input prompts and responses for debugging, but sensitive data redaction is a thing — we can redact or strip PII at ingestion and support configurable retention per customer. for customers with strict requirements we offer per-route logging configuration and can minimize storage of raw text.
[05:30] Sasha: legal hold and e-discovery — can you export logs on demand and does your export pipeline preserve integrity for audits?
[05:40] Mateo: exports are tamper-evident with signed manifests, and we provide streaming export to S3/GCS with object locking available on Dedicated/Private. we'll capture that in the docs we send.
[05:56] Evan: retention windows — default 90 days sounds ok for dev but we need a max retention cap of 1 year for some customers, and others require deletion after 30 days. is retention configurable by tenant?
[06:08] Priya: yes, retention is configurable. Hosted has standard tiers (30, 90, 365) and Dedicated/Private allow arbitrary retention policies and legal hold exemptions.
[06:25] Sasha: encryption in transit — TLS 1.2/1.3 ok? mutual TLS for internal backplane?
[06:32] Priya: we use TLS 1.3. mutual TLS for internal service-to-service is supported in Private deployments. for Hosted/Dedicated we use strong TLS with client cert options available for private endpoints.
[06:48] Jordan: quick ask — are you planning to connect via VPC peering, PrivateLink, or open internet?
[06:55] Evan: prefer PrivateLink for lower blast radius.
[07:00] Priya: PrivateLink supported for Dedicated customers, and we can do VPC peering in Private/on-prem installs.
[07:12] Sasha: RBAC — need least privilege controls, separation of duties, audit of admin actions. how granular is the RBAC model?
[07:20] Priya: RBAC supports role tiers: org admin, security admin, devops, developer, readonly. roles map to resource scopes (projects, models, routes). we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning so you can sync groups from Okta/Azure AD. all admin actions are logged to the audit stream.
[07:45] Sasha: can we integrate with our existing SIEM and send admin log events in real time?
[07:52] Mateo: yes, streaming to SIEM via secure forwarder or pushing to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket is standard.
[08:05] Omar: procurement question — what's typical SLA for Dedicated and what liability for data breach?
[08:12] Jordan: Dedicated has a latency and uptime SLA we can share; liability and breach clauses are negotiable for enterprise contracts, and we include SOC2 artifacts and indemnities typical to our enterprise terms. i'll tee up legal on the contract template.
[08:30] Evan: do you retain any customer data for model training or eval? we need guarantee no training on customer data.
[08:38] Jordan: we do not use customer data to train our models. we have a strict no-customer-data-for-training policy unless explicitly opted-in and contracted. i'll include the data usage policy link.
[08:52] Sasha: zero trust principles — can you do customer-managed secrets and ephemeral tokens for requests?
[08:58] Priya: yes, short-lived tokens and request-level encryption are supported. for Dedicated/Private, we can integrate with your secret manager and rotate keys on your schedule.
[09:12] Marie: performance: if we go Dedicated in eu-west and pin to small model variant, what's a realistic 99p latency and cost per 1k tokens?
[09:22] Priya: depends on model family and quantization; typical 99p for smaller llama-like models on Dedicated can be 300-700ms for non-streamed responses. cost per 1k tokens depends on the model; we'll propose targets in the POC scope.
[09:40] Evan: latency is a bit fuzzy; can we run an internal benchmark with our payload shapes?
[09:46] Priya: absolutely — POC includes benchmark harness, sample payloads, and synthetic concurrency tests.
[09:54] Sasha: regulatory — do you have EU data processing addendum and standard contractual clauses?
[10:00] Jordan: yes, we provide DPA with SCCs and can support data processing localization for EU customers.
[10:10] Omar: procurement timeline — we prefer a four-week POC and then procurement in 6-8 weeks. does that fit your typical ramp?
[10:19] Jordan: that's reasonable. POC kickoff in 1-2 weeks pending docs exchange looks doable.
[10:30] Evan: curious about model version pinning and rollbacks — we need predictable outputs for customer-facing features.
[10:36] Priya: you can pin model versions per route, do canary rollouts, and automatic fallback policies to older model variants if regressions are detected. these actions are audited.
[10:50] Sasha: evidence for audits — do you have SOC2 bridge letters and how recent is the audit?
[10:56] Jordan: our SOC2 Type II report ended June 2025 and we have a bridge letter; i'll share the redacted report and the bridge letter.
[11:10] Evan: for PII we need guarantees on scraping and retention, can you demonstrate how redaction pipeline works?
[11:18] Priya: in the POC we'll run your sample logs through our ingestion pipeline and show redaction outcomes; we also provide client side filtering patterns and pre-ingest transforms.
[11:35] Sasha: does Redwood offer HSM-backed key escrow or can we use our HSM?
[11:42] Priya: we support both — you can bring keys from your HSM into BYOK or we can store wrapping keys in our HSM with strict controls. for the strongest model we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed HSM.
[12:00] Jordan: small but important: incident response process and notification windows?
[12:06] Mateo: we commit to notify customers within 24 hours of any security incident affecting customer data, and we provide an incident postmortem and next steps. the contract spells notification SLAs.
[12:22] Sasha: do you have a bug bounty program or external disclosure channel?
[12:28] Jordan: yes, we run a bug bounty and coordinate with customers for escalations; we'll include the program link.
[12:40] Evan: network segmentation — can we host our models on Dedicated nodes that are network isolated?
[12:47] Priya: Dedicated nodes are tenant-isolated logically and can be placed into customer VPCs in Private deployments; network isolation in Dedicated has options depending on the cloud provider.
[13:05] Marie: what about key rotation frequency and crypto algorithm standards?
[13:12] Priya: we support RSA-2048/3072 and modern EC algorithms for signing and AES-256-GCM for data keys; key rotation can be automated quarterly or on your cadence.
[13:30] Sasha: for compliance we need audit trails of admin actions for 7 years — can you retain admin audit logs that long?
[13:38] Mateo: yes, with Dedicated/Private we can extend retention windows to multi-year with cold storage and object lock. hosted has standard tiers but can be negotiated for enterprise.
[13:55] Evan: tricky bit — we sometimes need to put certain customer subsets into legal hold indefinitely; can Redwood support per-tenant legal hold that overrides deletion policies?
[14:06] Priya: yes, legal hold is supported in Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we can create scoped exemptions but we need to validate scale and storage implications.
[14:20] Jordan: thinking of next steps — we'll share three artifacts: SOC2 Type II redacted report + pentest summary, an architecture note for Dedicated vs Private options, and a POC scope template.
[14:35] Omar: on pricing side, can you give a ballpark for Dedicated monthly commitment?
[14:42] Jordan: ballpark depends on GPU class and concurrency; typical entry commitment for mid-tier Dedicated is X per month — i'll send ranges in the follow-up.
[14:54] Evan: wanted to call out compliance with health data — some of our customers are in medtech; does Redwood support HIPAA workflows?
[15:02] Jordan: we can support HIPAA with a BAA on Dedicated/Private; Hosted requires review but many customers run PHI on Dedicated with contractual protections.
[15:18] Sasha: integration — SAML configuration for Okta, can we map groups to roles?
[15:24] Priya: yes SCIM + SAML mapping supported, we do group-to-role sync and can do automated deprovisioning.
[15:35] Marie: curious about disaster recovery and backup encryption — are backups encrypted at rest with separate keys?
[15:43] Mateo: backups are encrypted at rest and can be configured to use your KMS for wrapping. DR RPO/RTO depends on the deployment type and we can provide options.
[15:58] Evan: any historical incidents to disclose? high level only.
[16:03] Jordan: we've had a few low-severity incidents remediated quickly; none resulted in exfiltration of customer data. we'll include the high-level security summary in the packet.
[16:18] Sasha: for the POC we want a checklist: 1) SOC2 + pen test, 2) POC infra cost estimate, 3) region pinning, 4) KMS integration test, 5) retention configuration, 6) RBAC + SAML setup, 7) A sample payload benchmark.
[16:33] Priya: we'll author that checklist and include steps to provision a test tenant with PrivateLink endpoints and a demo key wrap with your KMS.
[16:50] Omar: timeline reminder — procurement needs a price and SOW to review; we need something before the end of august.
[16:58] Jordan: ok — action we'll target: send the docs within five business days.
[17:08] Evan: ping on BAA and DPA examples too.
[17:14] Jordan: will include DPA + SCCs and BAA template.
[17:20] Sasha: one more question — do you offer per-route redaction rules and can we supply regexes?
[17:28] Priya: yes, you can supply custom redaction regex and we can apply at the edge before logs are stored. we'll demo that in the POC.
[17:40] Marie: wrapping up — curious about support model during POC; do we get an SE assigned?
[17:47] Mateo: yes, SE support assigned, and we'll do two weekly syncs during the POC.
[17:55] Jordan: cool, let's recap next steps and owners.
[18:02] Jordan: recap: Jordan send SOC2 + pentest + DPA + BAA and architecture note; Priya send POC scope and checklist and schedule benchmark; Lumera share retention/regulatory docs and confirm stakeholders; set a tentative POC kickoff 2025-08-25.
[18:20] Evan: that works on our side.
[18:25] Omar: procurement will review once we get the price ranges.
[18:30] Jordan: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links to the docs and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.
[18:40] Sasha: thanks all.
[18:44] Marie: thanks.
[41:50] [call ends]

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels were estimated by the recorder; minor transcription errors expected (proper nouns, acronyms). references shared: SOC2 redacted report (link to be provided), pentest summary (link), POC checklist template (link), BYOK whitepaper (link).
